Draw multiple independent realizations of the branching structure

Source: R/sampling_branching.r
sample_branching_multi.Rd

Repeatedly calls sample_branching() to build a Monte Carlo ensemble of branching-structure realizations, for quantifying uncertainty in any summary that depends on the background/triggered classification of events (e.g. the number of background events per month, or their spatial concentration – see the package vignette on branching-structure UQ).

Usage

sample_branching_multi(
  bgprobs,
  pairs,
  pair_weights,
  n_samples = 100,
  seed = NULL,
  restore_rng = TRUE
)

Arguments

bgprobs, pairs, pair_weights

Passed to sample_branching() on every draw (fixed across draws – only the internal u ~ Uniform(0,1) draws differ between samples).

n_samples

Number of independent realizations to draw; default 100.

seed

Optional seed passed to set.seed() before drawing, for reproducibility. Default NULL (no seed set – uses the current RNG state).

restore_rng

Only used when seed is supplied. If TRUE (the default), the global random-number state is put back as it was before the call, so the seed affects only this call. If FALSE, the call leaves the generator in the state set.seed(seed) and its own draws produce, as earlier versions of the package did – useful for reproducing results from scripts that relied on that.

Value

A list of length n_samples, each element a "semihawkes_branching_sample" object from sample_branching().

See also

sample_branching() for a single draw, summarize_branching_samples() to extract per-sample summaries (e.g. number of background events) from the ensemble.

Examples

bgprobs <- c(1, 0.4, 0.5, 0.2)
pairs <- data.frame(i = as.integer(c(2, 3, 3, 4, 4)),
                    j = as.integer(c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3)))
pair_weights <- c(0.6, 0.3, 0.2, 0.5, 0.3)

samples <- sample_branching_multi(bgprobs, pairs, pair_weights,
                                  n_samples = 200, seed = 1)
length(samples)
#> [1] 200
summarize_branching_samples(samples)
#> <semihawkes_branching_summary>
#>   200 samples
#>   median background events: 2
#>   IQR: [2, 3]
